data.title: Preconditions for Ransomware Impact Are Present
data.summary:
The conditions that determine ransomware impact — broad file share access from ordinary
accounts, reachable backup infrastructure, and recoverable copies that can be deleted with
the same credentials — were all present.
data.description:
Ransomware outcomes are decided by the environment rather than by the malware. The
questions that matter are how much data a single compromised account can reach, whether
the recovery copies are reachable with the same credentials, and whether shadow copies and
snapshots can be removed by the account that encrypts.

In this environment each of those answers favoured the attacker. No deployment or
detonation was performed; the finding records the reachability and the control state
observed, which is what determines blast radius.

Stated this way it is also actionable without reference to any particular malware family,
and it remains valid as those families change.
data.recommendation:
* Restrict file share access so no ordinary account can reach data across the whole estate;
  measure the reachable volume per account.
* Hold at least one backup copy that is immutable or offline and cannot be reached with
  production credentials.
* Separate backup infrastructure credentials entirely from the production domain.
* Alert on bulk file modification rates and on deletion of shadow copies or snapshots.
* Test restoration at realistic scale rather than testing that backups complete.
data.short_recommendation: Hold an immutable backup copy and limit per-account reach to file shares.
